transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-02-20 11:10am PT, 52 minutes. Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Lucas Rivera (Redwood SE), Alex Reyes (CTO - Ramora Health), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Tom Ellis (DevOps), Samir (Security).

Summary (auto): High-level discovery on integration patterns for Ramora's healthcare chatbot and batch-embedding pipeline. Primary concerns: latency SLOs for triage assistant, data residency and KMS, gateway/proxy architecture to multiplex across Hosted/Dedicated, rate limits and quotas for multi-tenant workloads, and observability hooks for tracing tokens and errors. Action items captured.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for carving out the time, I'll kick us off. Quick agenda - run through current infra, integration options (SDK, gateway, langchain/llamaindex), security concerns, then next steps.
00:18 Alex Reyes: Sure, appreciate it. Short background: Ramora Health runs a triage assistant plus a separate batch embedding pipeline for clinical search. We need low latency for triage (p95 < 300ms ideally), and strict PHI controls. We're evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs a private VPC.
00:36 Jordan Patel: Great, thanks Alex. Quick clarifying q — are you planning to route all traffic through a single gateway in front of Redwood or have split routes per team?
00:45 Alex Reyes: We'll probably split. Triage gets priority, other stuff like batch embeddings can be async. We want per-route quotas because the clinical team will burn tokens differently than analytics.
00:58 Priya Singh: also, our devs use LangChain and LlamaIndex heavily — we need to know how well Redwood SDK maps to those libraries and whether we can run the request through our own proxy/gateway for centralized auth and rate limiting.
01:12 Jordan Patel: Totally. Our SDKs have first-class LangChain hooks; we surface a low-level HTTP/REST client and SDK wrappers that work with both LangChain and direct calls. For LlamaIndex, folks use embeddings + retrieval — the SDK supports batched embeddings and streaming. Small caveat: when you add a gateway proxy layer you'll need to preserve streaming semantics or swamp the latency.
01:36 Tom Ellis: When you say preserve streaming semantics, you mean chunking the response as it's generated? That can be tricky with some gateways which buffer.
01:44 Lucas Rivera: Right — if your gateway does full-response buffering, you'll lose the early tokens and increase tail latency. For triage we recommend a passthrough mode for streaming routes, or an edge config that forwards chunks to the client.
01:59 Samir: Security quick note: we require KMS-backed envelope encryption for keys, audit logs for every token request, and SAML SSO. Are those supported in Hosted?
02:10 Maya Chen: Short answer: yes for Hosted we provide SOC 2 reports, audit logs, and integrate with customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SSO and standard audit logs but for customer-managed KMS and strict VPC-only egress you'd look at Dedicated or Private.
02:28 Alex Reyes: So for PHI workloads, likely Dedicated or Private. But we need to understand the tradeoffs on cost and on latency. We can't have large variance in p95.
02:38 Jordan Patel: Understood. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — predictability on latency, and we can pin model versions. Private brings the control plane into your VPC and can be on-prem. Cost-wise Dedicated has a commit model; Hosted is pay-as-you-go and cheaper for lower steady-state. We'll send a TCO sheet.
02:55 Priya Singh: On the gateway/proxy question: can Redwood accept calls from our internal gateway and route to hosted/dedicated based on policy? e.g., some paths go to dedicated for low latency and others fall back to hosted?
03:08 Jordan Patel: Yep — smart routing is supported. You can front requests with your gateway and tag them; policy-based routing will hit different model variants and deployment targets. We also have automatic fallback to compatible variants when capacity's constrained. We'll need header-based routing to be enabled on your proxy.
03:24 Tom Ellis: Are there rate limits per API key? We have multiple teams with different budgets and we want per-route quotas and burst settings.
03:31 Maya Chen: We support token-level quotas per API key and per-route rate limits; for Dedicated you can configure burst capacity and autoscaling rules per pool. There is also token accounting in the console so you can see who consumed what.
03:45 Priya Singh: Regarding observability hooks — we need trace IDs from our app through Redwood and back into our Datadog traces. How does that work?
03:54 Lucas Rivera: We inject tracing headers and provide per-request trace IDs. The console has per-route dashboards and you can export logs/traces with a retention policy or push to your SIEM via integrations. There are also token-level cost breakdowns. Sometimes the auto-transcribed names of endpoints get munged, so keep structured route names.
04:15 Alex Reyes: For the embedding pipeline — we process millions of rows nightly. How does batching / quantization suggestions work?
04:24 Jordan Patel: Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization profiles based on workload characteristics. For embeddings we can do large gpus with fp16 or int8 quant modes if acceptable, which reduces cost significantly. We'll want sample traces so Optimize can generate recommendations.
04:38 Priya Singh: We also use cached retrieval — do you support prefix/KV cache? We want warm-start for patient-specific context.
04:45 Jordan Patel: Yes, KV cache (sometimes transcribed as kay vee cash in older transcripts) and prefix caching are supported. For private deployments you can control where the cache lives. For hosted we do managed KV cache but offer sticky session options.
05:00 Alex Reyes: Any limits on model size or specific kernels? We rely on Llama 2-70b hf variants for some internal experiments.
05:08 Lucas Rivera: We onboard Llama 2 and other open models; kernel selection is handled by the runtime. For huge models we recommend Dedicated unless latency requirements are very tight and you have budget.
05:18 Samir: Compliance — we need to see SOC 2 plus penetration testing attestation and encryption key lifecycle docs.
05:24 Maya Chen: We'll share the security pack. For Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your HSM/KMS and provide audit hooks.
05:31 Alex Reyes: Ok, practical next steps — we'd like a short perf POC: triage route hitting Dedicated capacity with streaming preserved, and an embeddings batch job against hosted/dedicated to compare cost.
05:43 Jordan Patel: Sounds good. I'll put together a POC checklist and infra template. We'll want sample prompts (Priya to supply) and a traffic shape (Tom). We'll run a 5-day test and capture p50/p95, token cost, and error rates.
05:56 Priya Singh: For the sample prompts I'll anonymize PHI, but they'll keep typical token lengths.
06:03 Tom Ellis: On our side, need a matrix of firewall rules and peering info so we can test VPC peering.
06:12 Maya Chen: Great. I'll send the TCO and the security docs. Can we agree on dates? Jordan, aim to kick the POC week of 2/24?
06:21 Jordan Patel: Yes, Jordan: agree. Will prepare infra checklist and perf plan by 2/27.
06:26 Alex Reyes: That works. Anything else?
06:29 Maya Chen: One last thought — pricing question: is streaming charged differently?
06:33 Lucas Rivera: Streaming is billed per token like other calls; the unit economics are similar but you may use fewer tokens due to partial responses in some flows. We'll include sample pricing rows.
06:44 Alex Reyes: Awesome. Thanks team.

Closing recap (auto): Redwood and Ramora aligned on POC scope: 1) Dedicated streaming triage perf test, 2) embeddings batch cost comparison, 3) share security & TCO docs. Owners and due dates in action items.
